coverage_note: Read in full: §§ 8, 11, 13, 16, 21, 24, 37, 39, 40 and 45 (Chapters One to Three, Five and Six). Not read: the Introduction, §§ 9-10, 12, 14-15, 17-20, 22-23, 25-36, 38, 41-44, 46-66 and the Third Section, among them § 23, § 25, § 28, § 29 and § 63, which carry 33-43 term hits each.

units.claim: When an intuition joins a merely symbolic expression afterward, a descriptively peculiar fulfilment-consciousness arises in which the meaning act finds fulfilment in the intuiting act as an aiming intention.
units.quote: When this event occurs, we experience a descriptively peculiar *fulfilment-consciousness* (*Erfüllungsbewußtsein*): the act of pure meaning finds, in the manner of an *aiming intention*, a fulfilment in the intuiting act.

units.claim: Static fulfilment is distinguished from dynamic fulfilment as a resting being-fulfilled and a being-in-coincidence, possibly with no preceding stage of unfulfilled intention.
units.quote: The fulfilment of the intention is here not a *process of self-fulfilling* but a resting *being-fulfilled*; not a *coinciding* but a *being-in-coincidence* (*in Deckung Sein*).

units.claim: What is called fulfilment with reference to the acts is, with reference to their objects, identity-consciousness or an act of identification.
units.quote: what we phenomenologically characterize, with reference to the acts, as *fulfilment* is, with reference to the bilateral objects — the intuited object on the one side, the thought object on the other — to be expressed as *identity-experience, identity-consciousness, act of identification*

units.claim: Disappointment is the excluding opposite of fulfilment and is not a privation of fulfilment but a new descriptive fact, a form of synthesis as peculiar as fulfilment.
units.quote: The mostly negative expression usually serving here — e.g., *non-fulfilment* — means no mere privation of fulfilment, but a new descriptive fact, a form of synthesis as peculiar as fulfilment.

units.claim: Conflict is not coordinate with fulfilment: an intention is disappointed in the manner of conflict only as part of a more comprehensive intention whose complementary part is fulfilled.
units.quote: *an intention disappoints itself in the manner of conflict only by being a part of a more comprehensive intention whose complementary part fulfils itself.* With simple or isolated acts, therefore, there can be no talk of conflict.

units.claim: Objectifying acts could be defined as those whose fulfilment-synthesis has the character of identification and whose disappointment-synthesis has the character of distinction.
units.quote: Accordingly we could outright *define* the objectifying acts as those whose fulfilment-synthesis has the character of *identification* (whose disappointment-synthesis, then, the character of *distinction*)

units.claim: Wish-fulfilment is founded in an identification but not exhausted by it, and speaking of satisfaction or fulfilment outside the sphere of feeling-intentions is only a simile.
units.quote: It is only a *simile* when we like to speak of satisfaction — indeed even of fulfilment — outside the sphere of the *Gemüt*\-intentions (intentions of feeling).

units.claim: Fulfilment is narrowed from identification in general to those identifications that bring the intention nearer to the knowledge-goal, in which a more or less perfect intuitivization takes place.
units.quote: in every fulfilment there takes place a more or less perfect *intuitivization* (*Veranschaulichung*). What the intention indeed means, but makes presentational in more or less improper or inadequate fashion, the fulfilment

units.claim: The fulfilment-relation is a relation of increase whose series points to an ideal limit, the adequate self-presentation of the object of knowledge.
units.quote: every such increase-series points to an *ideal limit* (*ideale Grenze*), or already realizes it in its end-member, which sets to all increase an unsurpassable goal: the goal of *absolute knowledge*, of the *adequate self-presentation* of the object of knowledge.

units.claim: Examples from mere imagination show that the character of fulfilment does not presuppose the positing-quality in either the intending or the fulfilling act.
units.quote: the character of fulfilment does *not* presuppose what is reckoned to the *logical* concept of knowledge — namely the *positing-quality* (*Setzungsqualität*), both in the intending and in the fulfilling acts.

units.claim: Signitive intentions are in themselves empty and lack any fullness, which only the intuitive presentation brings to them through identification.
units.quote: Rather, the signitive presentation lacks for itself *any* fullness; only the intuitive presentation brings it *to* it and, through the identification, *into* it. The signitive intention merely *points to* the object

units.claim: The distinction between mere identification and fulfilment is traced back to identity-syntheses of acts without fullness, or to enrichment of fullness accompanied by simultaneous emptying.
units.quote: fulfilment (enrichment of fullness) does take place, but under simultaneous emptying, under surrender of already present fullness, so that no pronounced and pure increase-consciousness comes about.

units.claim: The fulfilment-increase has a concluding goal, a definitive and ultimate fulfilment in which representing and represented content are identically one and adaequatio rei et intellectus is established.
units.quote: a *definitive and ultimate fulfilment* (*endgültige und letzte Erfüllung*). The intuitive content of this concluding presentation is the *absolute sum of possible fullness*; the intuitive representant is the *object itself, as it is in itself*.

units.claim: Truth in the first sense is the full agreement between meant and given, experienced in evidence understood as the actual performance of adequate identification.
units.quote: *the full agreement between meant and given as such*. This agreement is *experienced* in evidence, insofar as evidence is the actual performance of the adequate identification.

units.claim: Because categorially formed meanings also find fulfilment, every act fulfilling as confirming self-presentation is to be called perception and every fulfilling act intuition.
units.quote: The essential like-kindedness of the *fulfilment-function*, and of all the ideal relations lawfully connected with it, makes it unavoidable to designate every act fulfilling in the manner of *confirming self-presentation* as *perception*, every fulfilling act überhaupt as *intuition*
